topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course structure, and the learning objectives regarding cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer and mutation sources
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by mutations from intrinsic, inherited, and environmental origins.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens, risk perceptions, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey environmental risk factors, address public perceptions regarding cancer randomness versus causation, and examine geographical epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents in oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the oncogenic mechanisms of infectious pathogens and illustrate multi-factorial viral carcinogenesis through the case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and xenobiotic metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical agents undergo xenobiotic metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor initiation and promotion mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate between mutagenic initiation and non-mutagenic tumor promotion mediated by inflammatory and signaling pathways.

topics.label: Host susceptibility factors and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how host developmental stages influence susceptibility to carcinogens and summarize the key mechanisms of DNA damage.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposures and evaluate mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and everyday risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing key themes and discussing how individuals and societies balance carcinogenic risks against benefits in daily life.
